en: Proverbs 22

p.src: 1  A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favor is better than silver and gold.

en: A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favor is better than silver and gold.
u.src: 1  A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favor is better than silver and gold.

p.src: 2  The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is the maker of them all.

en: The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is the maker of them all.
u.src: 2  The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is the maker of them all.

p.src: 3  A prudent man sees danger and hides himself; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.

en: A prudent man sees danger and hides himself; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
u.src: 3  A prudent man sees danger and hides himself; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.

p.src: 4  The result of humility and the fear of the LORD is wealth, honor, and life.

en: The result of humility and the fear of the LORD is wealth, honor, and life.
u.src: 4  The result of humility and the fear of the LORD is wealth, honor, and life.

p.src: 5  Thorns and snares are in the path of the wicked; whoever guards his soul stays far from them.

ja: には、いばらとわながある。
en: Thorns and snares are in the path of the wicked; whoever guards his soul stays far from them.
u.src: 5  Thorns and snares are in the path of the wicked; whoever guards his soul stays far from them.

p.src: 6  Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.

en: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.
u.src: 6  Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.

p.src: 7  The rich rule over the poor. The borrower is servant to the lender.

en: The rich rule over the poor. The borrower is servant to the lender.
u.src: 7  The rich rule over the poor. The borrower is servant to the lender.

p.src: 8  He who sows wickedness reaps trouble, and the rod of his fury will be destroyed.

en: He who sows wickedness reaps trouble, and the rod of his fury will be destroyed.
u.src: 8  He who sows wickedness reaps trouble, and the rod of his fury will be destroyed.

p.src: 9  He who has a generous eye will be blessed, for he shares his food with the poor.

en: He who has a generous eye will be blessed, for he shares his food with the poor.
u.src: 9  He who has a generous eye will be blessed, for he shares his food with the poor.

p.src: 10  Drive out the mocker, and strife will go out; yes, quarrels and insults will stop.

en: Drive out the mocker, and strife will go out; yes, quarrels and insults will stop.
u.src: 10  Drive out the mocker, and strife will go out; yes, quarrels and insults will stop.

p.src: 11  He who loves purity of heart and speaks gracefully is the king’s friend.

en: He who loves purity of heart and speaks gracefully is the king’s friend.
u.src: 11  He who loves purity of heart and speaks gracefully is the king’s friend.

p.src: 12  The LORD’s eyes watch over knowledge, but he frustrates the words of the unfaithful.

en: The LORD’s eyes watch over knowledge, but he frustrates the words of the unfaithful.
u.src: 12  The LORD’s eyes watch over knowledge, but he frustrates the words of the unfaithful.

p.src: 13  The sluggard says, “There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the streets!”

en: The sluggard says, “There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the streets!”
u.src: 13  The sluggard says, “There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the streets!”

p.src: 14  The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit. He who is under the LORD’s wrath will fall into it.

en: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit. He who is under the LORD’s wrath will fall into it.
u.src: 14  The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit. He who is under the LORD’s wrath will fall into it.

p.src: 15  Folly is bound up in the heart of a child; the rod of discipline drives it far from him.

ja: に結びついているが、 訓練のむちがそれを
en: Folly is bound up in the heart of a child; the rod of discipline drives it far from him.
u.src: 15  Folly is bound up in the heart of a child; the rod of discipline drives it far from him.

p.src: 16  Whoever oppresses the poor for his own increase and whoever gives to the rich, both come to poverty.

ja: も、 どちらも貧しさに至る。
en: Whoever oppresses the poor for his own increase and whoever gives to the rich, both come to poverty.
u.src: 16  Whoever oppresses the poor for his own increase and whoever gives to the rich, both come to poverty.

p.src: 17  Turn your ear, and listen to the words of the wise. Apply your heart to my teaching.

en: Turn your ear, and listen to the words of the wise. Apply your heart to my teaching.
u.src: 17  Turn your ear, and listen to the words of the wise. Apply your heart to my teaching.

p.src: 18  For it is a pleasant thing if you keep them within you, if all of them are ready on your lips.

en: For it is a pleasant thing if you keep them within you, if all of them are ready on your lips.
u.src: 18  For it is a pleasant thing if you keep them within you, if all of them are ready on your lips.

p.src: 19  I teach you today, even you, so that your trust may be in the LORD.

ja: 、私はほかならぬあなたに教える。
en: I teach you today, even you, so that your trust may be in the LORD.
u.src: 19  I teach you today, even you, so that your trust may be in the LORD.

p.src: 20  Haven’t I written to you thirty excellent things of counsel and knowledge,

ja: 私はあなたのために、助言と知識について、 三十のすぐれたことを
en: Haven’t I written to you thirty excellent things of counsel and knowledge,
u.src: 20  Haven’t I written to you thirty excellent things of counsel and knowledge,

p.src: 21  To teach you truth, reliable words, to give sound answers to the ones who sent you?

ja: 真実で信頼できる言葉をあなたに教えるため。 あなたを
わした者たちに確かな
en: To teach you truth, reliable words, to give sound answers to the ones who sent you?
u.src: 21  To teach you truth, reliable words, to give sound answers to the ones who sent you?

p.src: 22  Don’t exploit the poor because he is poor; and don’t crush the needy in court;

ja: しさにつけ込んで搾取するな。 乏しい者を法廷で踏みにじってはならない。
en: Don’t exploit the poor because he is poor; and don’t crush the needy in court;
u.src: 22  Don’t exploit the poor because he is poor; and don’t crush the needy in court;

p.src: 23  for the LORD will plead their case, and plunder the life of those who plunder them.

en: for the LORD will plead their case, and plunder the life of those who plunder them.
u.src: 23  for the LORD will plead their case, and plunder the life of those who plunder them.

p.src: 24  Don’t befriend a hot-tempered man. Don’t associate with one who harbors anger,

ja: と友になってはならない。 憤りを抱く
と交わってはならない。
en: Don’t befriend a hot-tempered man. Don’t associate with one who harbors anger,
u.src: 24  Don’t befriend a hot-tempered man. Don’t associate with one who harbors anger,

p.src: 25  lest you learn his ways and ensnare your soul.

ja: の命をわなにかけないために。
en: lest you learn his ways and ensnare your soul.
u.src: 25  lest you learn his ways and ensnare your soul.

p.src: 26  Don’t you be one of those who strike hands, of those who are collateral for debts.

en: Don’t you be one of those who strike hands, of those who are collateral for debts.
u.src: 26  Don’t you be one of those who strike hands, of those who are collateral for debts.

p.src: 27  If you don’t have means to pay, why should he take away your bed from under you?

ja: 支払う手段がないなら、 なぜ自分の
り上げられなければならないのか。
en: If you don’t have means to pay, why should he take away your bed from under you?
u.src: 27  If you don’t have means to pay, why should he take away your bed from under you?

p.src: 28  Don’t move the ancient boundary stone which your fathers have set up.

en: Don’t move the ancient boundary stone which your fathers have set up.
u.src: 28  Don’t move the ancient boundary stone which your fathers have set up.

p.src: 29  Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve kings. He won’t serve obscure men.

ja: たちに仕える。 名もない者たちには仕えない。
en: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve kings. He won’t serve obscure men.
u.src: 29  Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve kings. He won’t serve obscure men.
